The firmament, as described in Genesis 1:6–8, is most commonly interpreted in Christian teaching as the sky or the expanse of the heavens that God created to separate the waters above from the waters below. This symbolizes the ordered structure of creation and the boundary between the earthly realm and the heavenly realm.

The biblical passages most often cited to support this are Genesis 1:6–8, Psalm 19:1 (“The heavens declare the glory of God; the firmament shows His handiwork”), and Ezekiel 1:22–26, where the firmament is depicted as a crystal-like expanse above the throne of God.
